17.t: Working with data: wire length and resistance
q: Read the resistance of 60 cm of thin wire.
Describe the relationship between length and resistance.
Resistance is directly proportional to length: double the length, double the resistance.
Compare the two wires at 100 cm and explain the difference.
Thin 5.6, thick 1.4 Ω: the thick wire has a quarter of the resistance. It has four times the cross-section area, so more room for electrons to flow.
Explain why a kettle’s cable is thicker than a phone charger’s.
A kettle draws a large current; a thick wire has low resistance, so it heats up less and does not overheat or melt its insulation.
